title: auth.user.role_changed payload
description:
Payload for `auth.user.role_changed`, published by Auth when an administrator changes which roles a membership holds (FR-30).

**A membership's roles, not a user's.** The routing key says `user` because FR-34.1 names it that way, and the distinction matters more than the name: roles are per organisation (ADR-0016), so this says nothing about the same person's standing anywhere else. A consumer that caches "what can this user do" without an organisation beside it will get this wrong.

Both the old and the new list are carried. A consumer holding no projection cannot diff, and the interesting question — was privilege *reduced* — is unanswerable from the new list alone. Auth asks it too: a reduction ends that organisation's sessions immediately (FR-9.3), because fifteen minutes of a permission you have just taken away is not taking it away.

The file name is the routing key — `SchemaDiscovery` keys the catalog by it.

user_id.description: Platform-wide user identity, as a string.

org_id.description: The organisation whose membership changed, matching the envelope's own `org_id`.

sessions_revoked.description: How many refresh-token families were ended in this organisation. Non-zero only when the change removed a permission; adding one revokes nothing, because logging somebody out in order to *give* them access is hostile and the next token refresh picks it up anyway.
